m1_desc: Hanging mass on the left side of the Atwood pulley
m2_desc: Hanging mass on the right side of the Atwood pulley
pulleyMass_desc: Mass of the rotating cylindrical pulley wheel
pulleyMass_real: Rotational inertia of the pulley reduces system linear acceleration
frictionTorque_desc: Rotational friction torque from axle bearings
frictionTorque_real: Energy dissipation in axle rotation reducing net acceleration

formulas.atwoodAccExpl: System acceleration in the absence of pulley mass and friction is the mass difference divided by total mass times gravity.
formulas.atwoodTensionExpl: Tension in a light, inextensible rope over a frictionless massless pulley is uniform on both sides.
formulas.realInertiaExpl: Pulley rotational inertia I = 0.5 M_p R^2 adds equivalent mass equal to half the pulley mass into system denominator.
formulas.maExpl: Ratio of output resistance force to input effort force (IMA = count of supporting strands in pulleys, or effort arm / load arm in levers).

steps.step1Title: Step 1: Static Equilibrium with Equal Masses
steps.step1Instr: Set both m1 and m2 to equal values of 4.0 kg and press Play.
steps.step1Hint: In this state, net acceleration is zero and string tension exactly balances each hanging weight.
steps.step2Title: Step 2: Generate Acceleration via Mass Imbalance
steps.step2Instr: Change m2 to 5.0 kg and m1 to 3.0 kg, then observe the acceleration.
steps.step2Hint: Verify how the simulated acceleration matches the theoretical formula a = (m2 - m1)/(m1 + m2) * g.
steps.step3Title: Step 3: Compare Ideal and Real Physical Modes
steps.step3Instr: Switch to Real mode to observe how pulley rotational inertia and axle friction damp the acceleration.
steps.step3Hint: In Real mode, rope tensions on both sides of the pulley differ due to net torque required to angularly accelerate the wheel.
